description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

This club is made from the cleaned and polished femur of a giant, crafted finely into a usable two-handed club. Its tapered hilt is wrapped in stained leather. Fastened to the top of the club is a large troll skull with several monstrous teeth embedded into it like a bone morningstar, giving the weapon a grim appearance. The club is imbued with elemental power from the animus used to power the weapon, which causes it to crackle with elemental power.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic greatclub, and you have Advantage on attack rolls made against Giants.
While attuned to this club you deal an additional **2d6** damage of the type associated with the elemental dust infused into it.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Giant Femur Club requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Giant Animus from a Troll
• **[Bone]**: Skull from a Troll
• **[Bone]**: Bone from a Giant
• **[Dust]**: Elemental Dust from a Troll
• **[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Teeth from a Giant, Beast, or Monstrosity

The dust component determines the additional damage the club deals. For example, dust from a __Storm Troll__ deals Lightning damage, and dust from an __Eldritch Troll__ causes the club to deal Necrotic damage.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
Your Dexterity score is 19 while you wear these ratling hide gloves. They have no effect on you if your Dexterity is 19 or higher without them.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Gloves of Ratling Agility requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Hair]**: Fur from any Ratling
• **[Hide]**: Skin from any Ratling
• **[Organ]**: Guts from any Monstrosity
When you consume this potion, you immediately gain the benefits of a Long Rest.
Once you consume a Greater Rejuvenation Potion, you can't benefit from consuming another until you finish 3d6 Long Rests.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Greater Rejuvenation Potion requires a Legendary Workshop and the following Legendary Components:

This crimson and gold hooded cape is fitted with the feathers of fallen Harpies and dyed in their blood, this grants the wearer some resistance to the songs of Harpies. The cape is then infused with the dust of a fey creature which grants it a powerful anti-charm effect powered by an animus.
While wearing this cape, you have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Hazewind Cape requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Animus from a Harpy
• **[Dust]**: Fey Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Harpy
• **[Hair]**: Feathers from a Harpy
• **[Hide]**: Skin

This helm is forged in fires ignited with elemental dust, using plates from a construct and the heart of a red dragon. The plates are then soaked in elemental fluid before having an animus gem installed that contains the energy of a Fire Giant.

While your Rage is active, you gain Resistance to Fire damage. In addition, once per turn, while you are Raging, when you hit a target with a Melee weapon that benefitted from your Reckless Attack feature, the target becomes Burning (2d4 Fire).

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Helm of Burning Rage requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Animus from a Fire Giant
• **[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
• **[Hide]**: Plates
• **[Organ]**: Heart from a Red Dragon
Structured from the fur and skin of a monstrosity and the horns of a fiend, and coated in the dust of fey creatures, this mantle is imbued with charming energies.
Your Charisma score is 19 while you wear this magic cape. It has no effect on you if your Charisma is 19 or higher without it.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Mantle of Otherworldly Charisma requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Hair]**: Fur from a Monstrosity
• **[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Horns from a Fiend
• **[Dust]**: Fey Dust

This magic mask is made from the skull of a particular monstrosity (with a Challenge Rating of 6 or lower). The skull is carved into a mask, engraved with aberrant dust, and then boiled in a vat of mimic mucus, the flesh of a doppelganger, and acidic bile. Finally, a vessel containing the animus of any creature with the Shapechanger trait is placed upon the forehead of the mask, channeling its shapechanging magic.
While attuned to the mask, you can expend two uses of your Wild Shape feature to transform into the monstrosity associated with the mask, instead of a Beast.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Mask of Monstrous Forms requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Animus from a creature that has the Shapechanger trait
• **[Bones]**: Skull of a Monstrosity*
• **[Dust]**: Aberrant Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Acidic Bile
• **[Fluid]**: Mucus from a Mimic
• **[Organ]**: Flesh from a Doppelganger
** The Monstrosity used for this mask determines the form of the shapechange.*
This pelt cape is made from the fur of a Garmyr stitched carefully into the leathers of a ratling, decorated with the talons of a harpy, and polished to a shine with contaminated ichor.
While you are attuned to this pelt and are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, your allies have Advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Pelt of the Pack Lord requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Monstrosity Animus
• **[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
• **[Hair]**: Fur from a Garmyr
• **[Hide]**: Skin from a Ratling
• **[Natural Weapon]**: Claws from a Harpy

The jeweled pendant has 3 charges, which are replenished when you finish a Long Rest. When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, you can use a Reaction to expend 1 charge from the pendant to gain resistance to that damage type until the end of your next turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Pendant of Prismatic Protection requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus from an Elemental
• **[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Any two Elemental Fluids from different Elementals

This sickly-looking potion contains a writhing mass of tentacles that animate and uncomfortably crawl down the imbiber's throat when consumed. The taste is pungent and fishy, and results in the sudden outbreak of random, but temporary, mutations.

When you consume this potion, you gain the effects of one randomly determined Mutation until you start a Short or Long Rest. You can roll on the Mutations table twice, choosing which mutation manifests. You don't gain any Contamination levels as a result of this Mutation. When the effect ends, your body returns to normal.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Potion of Controlled Mutation requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Animus from an Aberration
• **[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
• **[Organs]**: Any two Organs from an Aberration

When you hit with an attack as part of an Attack action using this magic dagger and apply your Sneak Attack to the damage roll, you can make an additional attack using this dagger as part of the same action. If that attack hits and meets the criteria for your Sneak Attack, you can apply half your Sneak Attack dice (rounded down) to the attack's damage.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Rat Tooth Dagger requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Fluid]**: Venom
• **[Hide]**: Bark
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Claws from a Ratling

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This magic shield is formed from the shell of an Anomollusk combined with leather from an aberration as its handle. It's fused together and coated in contaminated ichor and inset with a rare animus. Once complete, the shell gives off an otherworldly hue that shimmers in kaleidoscopic patterns. The shield can reflect attacks and magic.

When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, you can use your Reaction to cause the creature to take the same damage (you still take the damage).

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Reflector Shield requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Fluid]**: Contaminated Ichor
• **[Hide]**: Shell from an Anomollusk
• **[Hide]**: Skin from an Aberration
When you drink this bright purple potion, you immediately gain the benefits of a short rest.
After you consume a Rejuvenation Potion, you can't benefit from consuming another until you finish a 1d4 Long Rests.

description.name: Crafting

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Dust]**: Fey Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Any Elemental Fluid
• **[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Dragon
• **[Organ]**: Heart from a Fiend

These boots are crafted from the flesh and scales of a dragon and decorated with Harpy feathers and the webbed membranes of flying creatures. The soles are injected with goopy ooze, allowing their wearer to jump back in time and space.

You can use a Bonus Action on your turn to click the heels of these boots together. When you do, you teleport to the space you occupied at the start of your turn so long as it is currently unoccupied.

description.name: Crafting

When you roll damage for a spell of level 1 or higher, you can expend this scroll to re-roll a number of the damage dice up to the level of the spell cast. You must use the new rolls.

• **[Animus]**: Any
• **[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Fey, Dragon, or Giant
• **[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity

These steel arm blades are razor sharp, 4-foot-long scythes that are fastened to two locking bracers made of spinal bones. The fasteners are made from fine leather with steel buckles. Delerium crystals are embedded in the armbands, infusing the blades with energy.
These magic shortswords function as a pair and must be wielded together for their magic properties to function. Attuning to the shortswords counts as being attuned to one magic item.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these magic shortswords. While attuned to these weapons, you can activate the Nick mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with these weapons.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Scythed Arm Blades requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Bones]**: Spine
• **[Hide]**: Plates
• **[Hide]**: Skin from any Beast or Monstrosity
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Two Blades from a Reautomata

description.name: Light

That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
While wearing these supple leather boots, Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Swashbuckler's Boots requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any
• **[Dust]**: Fey Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
• **[Hide]**: Any

These leather gloves are outfitted with the talons of fallen beasts and stitched together with the arcane stitching of apothecary creations. The gloves are then empowered by elemental magic, reinforced with bone, and powered by an animus.
While wearing these gloves, you gain Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and your Unarmed Strikes deal an additional **1d6** Piercing damage on a hit.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Talon Gloves requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
• **[Hair]**: Stitches
• **[Hide]**: Skin
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Claws

This whip is made from the tentacles and guts of aberrant creatures, stitched to the webbed membranes of winged beasts and fused to the bark of a plant creature. Once the animus is placed, the tentacles begin to writhe and wriggle and the whip can latch and drag creatures along the ground with uncanny strength.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic whip, which has a reach of 20 feet.
Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with an attack using this weapon, you can pull it 10 feet towards you.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Tentacle Whip requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Hair]**: Stitches
• **[Hide]**: Bark
• **[Hide]**: Webbed Membrane
• **[Natural Weapons]**: Tentacles from an Aberration

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Slow
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

The inner workings of this clockwork device are formed from gears forged from magical constructs gathered around a focusing lens, held together carefully by the needles of magical creatures. The animus used harnesses the energy of The Algorithm, a being of order and consequence, whose control over time and space ripples from the strange clockworks of the medallion.
This medallion has 3 charges. It crumbles to dust when you expend the final charge.

You can expend 1 charge from the medallion to take an extra action on your turn. Each time you do, you can roll 1d6. On a 1, at the end of your turn, you become unstuck in time and space as the medallion casts the __Maze__ spell on you. On a 6, the medallion regains 1d3 charges.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating the Time Dilation medallion requires a Legendary Workshop and the following Legendary Components:

• **[Animus]**: Animus from The Algorithm*
• **[Hide]**: Plates from a Construct
• **[Natural Weapon]**: Any Needles
• **[Organ]**: Eye from a Construct

This potion is a bubbling, sickly, green-brown viscous soup that has the consistency of mucus. What appears to be the rotting eye of a troll floats in the potion. It smells acrid and nauseating and tastes even worse than it looks.
When you drink this potion, for the next minute, you regain 5 Hit Points at the start of your turn. The effects of this potion end early if you take Fire or Acid damage.

description.name: Crafting

• **[Animus]**: Fey Animus

• You gain Advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Charisma attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
• If damage reduces you to 0 Hit Points, you must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + half the damage taken, unless the damage is Radiant or from a Critical Hit. On a success, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead, and the effects of this potion end.
• The effects of this potion end early if you take Radiant damage or enter sunlight.

description.name: Crafting

• **[Animus]**: Undead Animus
• **[Dust]**: Undead Dust from any Vampire
• **[Fluid]**: Ectoplasm
• **[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Vampire
This wand is carved from magical bark, with the hair of an undead creature in its core and finished in goopy ooze.
Once per turn when you deal damage with a Warlock cantrip to a creature, you can make that creature Jinxed (1d4) until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Wand of Jinxes requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Fluid]**: Goopy Ooze
• **[Hair]**: Hair from an Undead
• **[Hide]**: Bark
Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature using a cantrip while holding this wand, one target of that cantrip takes an extra **1d4** damage of the type dealt by the spell.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Wand of the Precocious Apprentice requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any
• **[Bones]**: Bones from an Undead
• **[Dust]**: Fey Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Ectoplasm

This large greataxe is made from a blade taken off a Ripper and refitted into a housing made from the plates of constructs and reinforced with the rib bones of a monstrosity. The blade is equipped with a leather belt that connects to an elemental-fueled motor powered by a Very Rare Animus.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
Once on your turn when you hit a Bloodied creature using this weapon, you can make one additional attack with this weapon as part of the same action.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Whirling Bonesaw requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Bones]**: Ribs
• **[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
• **[Hide]**: Plates
• **[Hide]**: Skin from any Monstrosity
• **[Natural Weapon]**: Blade from a Ripper

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

name: Manual of Occult Anatomy +1
type: rare (requires attunement by an apothecary or warlock)

description.value: Filled with diagrams showing humans with alien features, this book of strange medical lore is written in monster-blood ink infused with draconic dust and then etched onto parchment pages made from aberration skin. The manuscript is bound in a scale-clad cover.

You can use this manual as a Spellcasting Focus for your Apothecary or Warlock spells. When you use the manual as a Spellcasting Focus, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs of your Apothecary or Warlock spells.

In addition, the book contains the knowledge of an Apothecary Esoteric Theory or Warlock Eldritch Invocation up to a level determined by the manual's rarity and chosen when the item is created, which you gain while you are attuned to it. This determines which class is required to attune to the item.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Manual of Occult Anatomy requires a Workshop and Components of equal rarity to the item created. The Components required are:

• **[Animus]**: Any Animus
• **[Dust]**: Any Dragon Dust
• **[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Monstrosity
• **[Hide]**: Scales
• **[Hide]**: Skin from an Aberration

description.value: Filled with diagrams showing humans with alien features, this book of strange medical lore is written in monster-blood ink infused with draconic dust and then etched onto parchment pages made from aberration skin. The manuscript is bound in a scale-clad cover.

In addition, the book contains the knowledge of an Apothecary Esoteric Theory or Warlock Eldritch Invocation up to a level determined by the manual's rarity and chosen when the item is created, which you gain while you are attuned to it. Because they have no hands, worgs cannot wield weapons in the same way that most player characters can. However, worgs can wield a specially designed Martial Melee weapon called "Steel Jaws." Only Worgs can wield Steel Jaws, fitting as they do over a Worg's teeth. A Worg cannot use its Bite trait while it is wielding Steel Jaws.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

The wit and wisdom of Beggar Dane is considered to be one of the national treasures of Breland. This small leatherbound book is a comprehensive, enchanted edition of his proverbs and advice. As a Magic action while holding this book, you can declare your desire for assistance with a particular task, causing the book to open to a page containing a quip or mote of wisdom that is strangely relevant to the situation at hand. You add 1d4 to the next ability check you make within the next minute. Once this property is used, you cannot benefit from any copy of *Beggar's Wisdom* until the next dawn.

Daff d'Jorasco's eclectic style of medicine produces similarly eclectic brews. This potion is a magic item. As a Bonus Action, you can drink it or administer it to another creature within 5 of yourself. The creature that drinks this potion must roll on the following table to determine the effect:

value.title: Potion Effects
rows: You gain the effects of the Detect Thoughts spell for 1 minute or until you lose your Concentration. The save DC is 13.
You gain the effects of the Haste spell for 1 minute or until you lose your Concentration.
You must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or suffer the effects of the Tasha's Hideous Laughter spell for 1 minute.

description.value: This desiccated Spell Scroll seems to draw the moisture from your fingertips. Its cipher is ineffable, and while its meaning becomes clear as you read the runes, clarity slips away should you try to transcribe it.

As a Magic action, you can use the scroll to cast __Control Water__ without providing any Material components. The spell save DC is 15. In addition to the usual effects of the __Control Water__ spell, any water manipulated by the spell is destroyed when the spell ends. Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and it crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll is not lost.

This scrap of paper bears a table with space for five names. If you write a creature's name in one of the blank spaces on the table, it will shuffle the text to show their ranking as a duelist relative to all the other individuals named on the table. This appears to be calculated based on the number of duels the named individuals have won over the past year. The source of these scorecards and the rankings remains a mystery, but it appears to be linked to the Infinite Archive of Daanvi. Once all the spaces on the scorecard are filled, you cannot reveal the ranking of another name for 1 week, when all the names are magically erased.

This delicate Wand hums with bound potential, and seems drawn to your fingers. While attuned to it, you cannot be *Surprised*. Additionally, whenever you roll Initiative you can choose to immediately draw this wand (no action required). If you do so, you can roll 1d4 and add the total to your Initiative score, and all creatures within 5 feet of you take 1 Lightning damage.
This magic Shield resembles a wooden wagon wheel. Writing inscribed on its inner rim indicates the shield was crafted by Jury d'Cannith, Quickstone's premier artificer, to prove a point to her wife.

As a Bonus Action while holding this shield, you can grant Temporary Hit Points equal to your level to the humanoid creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that has the fewest Hit Points. If creatures you can see within range are tied for the fewest Hit Points, you can choose which of those creatures gains the Temporary Hit Points.

This 10-foot-wide, 10-foot-long, 6-inch-thick platform of wood and steel levitates 5 feet off the ground and remains horizontal so long as it is within 20 feet of an operational track of lightning rail conductor stones. The platform can carry up to 2000 pounds. If it becomes overloaded, it drops to the ground, unable to levitate.

The platform is equipped with a 'pump' in its center that can be used to move it along the track of conductor stones. As a Magic action, a creature touching the pump can expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to cause the platform to continuously move either forwards or backwards along the conductor stone track at a speed of 30 feet. A creature with the Mark of Passage does not need to expend a spell slot to cause the platform to move.

Once moving, the platform will move in the chosen direction for one hour, or until a creature touching the pump uses a Magic action to cause the platform to stop. If stopped in this way, a creature must expend another spell slot as a Magic action to start the platform moving again.

If the platform encounters an obstacle while moving, it will continue to push against the obstacle unless stopped with a Magic action. Obstacles that weigh less than the total weight of the platform and its cargo will be pushed in front of the platform.

This small embroidered pouch is said to contain the cast-off goods discarded by the Merchant of Misthaven, an archfey of Thelanis. When you reach into the pouch, you can pull out a random trinket (see page 46 of the 2024 version of the fifth edition Player's Handbook or any other random trinket table of your choice). A trinket pulled from this pouch disappears when you pull another trinket from the pouch.

Whenever you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher using this Rod as a Spellcasting Focus, you can choose to release its power in a thunderous burst. All creatures within 5 feet of you (including you) must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, affected creatures take **1d4** Thunder damage for each level of the spell you cast, and are Deafened until the end of their next turn.

Many of the discarded weapons of the Last War have found their way into the hands of the people of the Barrens. This sliver of a broken Siege Staff can deliver a powerful punch when it needs to, but ejects an exhaust of swirling dust when exerted.
This staff can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn.

When you cast a spell using this Staff as a Spellcasting Focus, you can expend 1 charge to gain a +1 bonus to all spell attack rolls you make for that spell. If you do so, the staff conjures a 5-foot diameter vortex of dust in your space. At the start of each of your turns, roll a d20 for each dust vortex the staff has created. On a roll of 11 or higher, the dust vortex moves 5 feet in a random direction. On a roll of 10 or less, the dust vortex disappears.

Any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of any of the dust vortexes must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, an affected creature takes **1d4** Bludgeoning damage and is Blinded until the end of its turn.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

Deven Sarkaas of Littlehand Haberdashers in Quickstone knows all too well how important it is to look one's best... and how 'best' can be very different depending on who (or what) you're meeting with. Deven stitched this fine cloak and sent it to Graywall to be enchanted, only to lose track of the garment on the return journey.

As a Bonus Action while wearing the cloak, you can speak its command word to transform your outfit into finely crafted garments appropriate to the culture of one creature of your choice that you can see. Regardless of its appearance, the outfit can't be anything but clothing. Although it can duplicate the look of other magical clothing, the outfit doesn't gain its magical properties.
This Dagger is said to have been created by Kethelrax the Cunning, the kobold warlord of Shaarat Kol. Its short, crimson blade resembles a red dragon's scale, and tiny flames dance along its edge.

While you are holding this Dagger, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells. Additionally, you can cast __Fire Bolt__ as a Magic action, using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (you choose when you Attune to the dagger) as the spellcasting ability.
Whenever you hit with a weapon attack using this Dagger, you can choose to deal Fire damage instead of Piercing damage.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

This pair of rough and ready War Picks are said to have been created by the first miners to quarry quickstone in the Barrens. They have long been passed around as heirlooms and rewards. These magical picks are a single magic item for the purposes of Attunement.
You gain the following benefits while wielding both picks:

• The picks have the Light weapon property.
• You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the picks.
• The picks have 3 charges, which they share. They regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.
• When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Shock, you can expend 1 charge as a bonus action to deal an additional **2d8** Lightning damage. A creature affected by this damage can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
• When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Ore, you can expend 1 charge to cast __Earth Tremor__ XGE as a Reaction, centered on the target.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Sap
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

This gold piece appears to be a normal coin, with the crown of Galifar on one side and the Octogram of the Sovereign Host on the other. However, when flipped, it will land with one of three different symbols showing, each corresponding to one of the patrons of the Three Faces of Coin: Kol Korran, Onatar, and Kol Turrant (the Keeper). When you flip the coin, you can will the coin to land displaying a face of your choice. Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

While this item doesn't require a command word or Attunement, the ability must be consciously triggered; if you've never used a Three-faced coin before, you must spend a Short Rest studying it to learn how to activate it. After being flipped, the coin returns to its usual two faces when a creature next touches it.

name: Thunder Coach
type: rare (requires attunement by a creature with the mark of passage)

description.value: The Thunder Coach is the workhorse of Orien's overland shipping, sometimes referred to as "galleons of the road." A product of the Twelve, it incorporated members of Kundarak, Cannith, and Orien in the design. A typical coach is a 10-foot-wide, 40-foot-long, 15-foot-high (including the wheels) vessel of wood and steel. When pulled by a large team (typically eight tribex), a coach can maintain a speed of up to five miles per hour. However, if someone with the Mark of Passage attunes to the coach and sits in the driver's seat, the full magic of the Thunder Coach comes into play. Under such conditions, four strong beasts can pull the coach at a steady pace of ten miles an hour. If it is moving along an Orien trade road, the effect is further amplified, allowing a top speed of 15 miles per hour. This requires the driver to remain seated and to maintain *Concentration*, as if casting a spell. However, beyond these limitations, they are capable of conversation and other actions.

The forward fifteen feet of the coach holds a small cabin for up to three crew members. The crew of a coach typically includes one marked driver and two crew members who serve as both guards and cargo haulers. One of these haulers is usually a Vadalis- trained (though unmarked) handler who cares for the beasts. The top of the coach has positions at the front and back where archers or wandslingers can be stationed with Half Cover.

A typical Thunder Coach has two cargo chambers; one magical and one mundane. The back gate of a Thunder Coach opens to grant access to an extradimensional space that functions in the same way as a Bag of Holding. When closed, the gate is typically sealed with an Arcane Lock linked to a password known to the driver. The mouth of the extradimensional space is 10-feet-wide by 10-feet-high. The size of the extradimensional space varies based on the model of the coach; the standard is 20-feet-wide, 15-feet-high, and 50-feet-deep. The system maintaining the extradimensional space takes up the final five feet of the coach.

Objects that produce extradimensional spaces (such as Bags of Holding, Portable Holes, or House Cannith's Crates of Containing) cannot cross the threshold of the rear compartment. For this reason, and to allow the transport of living creatures, the Thunder Coach also has a standard cargo compartment accessed from the side of the vehicle; this space is 10-feet-wide, 10-feet- high, and 20-feet-long.
One end of this heavy, black iron Rod glows as if hot. Rather than burning red and orange, it shines a sickly shade of purple.
While holding this Rod, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

Whenever you touch a creature with this Rod, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be branded with the mark of Tol Kharash, the overlord known as the Horned King. Whenever a branded creature makes an attack roll or a saving throw against being Frightened, the creature must roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll or saving throw. The brand lasts until the next dawn or it is removed with Remove Curse or Greater Restoration.

Red and black flames flicker behind the rough cut facets of this heavy demonglass shard. Memories of the Ages of Demons are bound within, and spellcasters who dare channel their magic through it find themselves and their targets visited by visions of that terrible past.

Whenever you cast a Divination spell using this Orb as a Spellcasting Focus, you can give up some of your life force to reduce the saving throw of one creature affected by your spell. Roll 1 to 4 d6s; the resulting total is how much Necrotic damage you take. This damage can't be reduced in any way. The target has its saving throw reduced by 1 for each **d6** of damage you take. You must decide how many dice to roll before the DM says whether the target succeeds or fails.

Tol Kharash, the Horned King, overlord of tyranny, demands that his minions revel in domination, fear, and the suffering of the downtrodden. During his campaigns in the Age of Demons, Tol Kharash shaped an artifact that would announce his coming across the Barrens; a harbinger of cruelty.

Kharash's Promise is a 3-foot long warhorn forged of demonglass and black iron. A trickle of boiling blood constantly drips from its widest end. While holding this Horn, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your Bard spells.

description.name: Random Properties.
description.value: This Artifact has the following random properties, which you can determine by rolling on the tables in the "Artifacts" section of the Dungeon Master's Guide:

• 2 minor beneficial properties
• 1 major beneficial property
• 2 minor detrimental properties

description.name: Surety of Dominance
description.value: While attuned to the warhorn, no creature can assert its influence over you. You cannot be Charmed or Frightened. If a creature targets you with a magical effect that would cause you to be Charmed or Frightened, that creature takes **4d10** Psychic damage.

description.name: Thaumaturgic Clarion
description.value: If you blow Kharash's Promise, the sound it produces can be heard by all creatures within 1 mile.

description.name: Promised End
description.value: As a Magic action when you blow the horn, you can choose one creature that you can see and that can hear the horn to suffer a painful and inevitable end. The target must make a DC 20 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by 1 at the start of each of its turns until it dies, you die, you are no longer on the same plane of existence as the target, or the effect is ended with a __Wish__ spell. Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until 13 days have passed.
As a Bonus Action while affected, the target can choose to confront the source of its inevitable end, teleporting to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

This colorful, jellyfish-like blob has been carefully cultivated by Quickstone's schoolmaster, Tragomir "Ink" Narathun, to impart a full curriculum to its host—though he has yet to convince anyone to partake. To attune to this item, you must hold it to one ear for the full Attunement period, during which time its stringy tentacles reach inside your ear canal and secure the aide in place. The symbiont does not impair your hearing while it is attached.

description.name: Spells
description.value: The symbiont has 4 charges. You can use a Magic action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: __Enhance Ability__ (2 charges) or __Comprehend Languages__ (1 charge).
The symbiont regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn.

description.name: Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The aide can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the aide ends, and it detaches from your ear.

This Plate Armor appears to be made of stone slabs carved with alien symbols. It is strangely warm to the touch. To attune to this item, you must wear it for the entire Attunement period, during which the stone plates fuse with your skin.

While wearing this armor, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class, and you have Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Additionally, the armor hardens under extreme impact; if you take 20 or more nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from one damage roll (after accounting for your Resistance), you are Petrified until the end of your next turn.

description.name: # Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The armor can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the armor ends, and it detaches from you.
The armor requires fresh blood be fed to it. Immediately after you finish any Long Rest, you must either feed half of your remaining Hit Dice to the armor (round up) or take 1 level of Exhaustion.

Despite being separated from its original owner, the lost arm of the daelkyr Orlassk can grant its wielder a sliver of the Lord of Stone's magic; enough power to reshape the world. To attune to this symbiont, you must hold it against one of your arms for the full Attunement period, during which time its stone skin softens and envelops your limb.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: This Artifact has the following random properties, which you can determine by rolling on the tables in the "Artifacts" section of the Dungeon Master's Guide:

• 2 minor beneficial properties
• 2 minor detrimental properties
• 1 major beneficial property
• 1 major detrimental property

description.name: # Voice of the Daelkyr
description.value: You can speak with any Aberration as if you shared a language.

description.name: # Command Aberration
description.value: As a Magic action, you can cast __Dominate Monster__ on an Aberration (save DC 18). Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

description.name: # Petrifying Touch
description.value: The power of the stone shaper flows from you—despite what you may will. Any creature that you touch with your stone fingertips is affected as if you had cast __Flesh to Stone__ (spell save DC 18). You do not need to concentrate on the effect, and you cannot choose to end it.

description.name: # Stone Speaking
description.value: As a Magic action, you imbue stones in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience, giving them the ability to communicate with you. You can question stones about events in the effects area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, items that might have been removed from the area, and other circumstances. If an earth elemental or Petrified creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language, but you gain no magical ability to influence it.

description.name: # Greater Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The arm can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. Your Attunement to the arm can only be ended by a __Wish__ spell.

This ancient, heavy marble torc is strangely warm to the touch. Though it resembles stone jewelry, the torc is in fact a simple symbiont which grants a limited form of control over earth and the ability to manipulate quickstone without the usual rituals. To attune to it, you must wear it around your neck for the full Attunement period, during which time it coils around your throat like a snake.
While wearing the torc, you can use a Magic action to transform a 5-foot cube of quickstone between its soft and wet forms, or irreversibly change it into its fixed form.

description.name: # Spells
description.value: As an Action, you can use the symbiote to cast __Mold Earth__ XGE or Meld into Stone. Once you use the torc to cast __Meld into Stone__, the spell can't be cast in this way until the next dusk.

description.name: # Symbiotic Nature
description.value: The torc can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your Attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your Attunement to the torc ends, and it uncoils from around your neck.

As a Bonus Action when you bark the command word, you can transform from your worg form into a goblin form with your choice of physical characteristics, including age, sex, skin color, hair color, and voice. While transformed, your size is Small and you lose your Quadruped and Bite traits. Otherwise, your statistics don't change.

You can maintain the transformation for up to 4 hours, all at once or in several shorter periods, each one using a minimum of 1 minute of the duration. The collar regains 2 hours of transformation time for every 12 hours it isn't in use.

While wearing this magical blindfold, you can see as if you were not wearing it, and you cannot be Blinded by magical effects. However, if you possess the Petrifying Gaze trait, you cannot use it while you are wearing the blindfold.

When you don the blindfold, you can choose to magically seal it in place by nominating yourself or a creature you can see to hold the seal's power. You cannot remove the blindfold until the creature speaks a chosen command word, you and the creature are at least 1 mile apart, or the creature dies.

name: Figurine of Wondrous Power, Byeshk Worg Pack

description.value: This set of four miniature worg statuettes is made from byeshk, a metal that is anathema to Aberrations. Each statuette is small enough to fit in a pocket. If you use a Magic action to speak the command word and throw one of the figurines to a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, the figurine becomes a living Worg for up to 1 hour. You can use one figurine or multiple simultaneously. If the space where a worg would appear is occupied by other creatures or objects, or if there isn't enough space for the worg, the figurine doesn't become a worg.
The worgs are Immune to Psychic damage, cannot be Charmed or Frightened, and their Bite attack deals an additional **2d6** damage against Aberrations.
The worgs are friendly to you and your companions. They understand your languages and obey your spoken commands. If you issue no commands, the worgs defend themselves but take no other actions.

At the end of the duration, the worgs revert to their figurine forms. A worg reverts to a figurine early if it drops to 0 Hit Points or if you use a Magic action to speak the command word again while touching it. When a worg becomes a figurine again, its property can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

This suit of Scale Mail is made from the metallic hide of a gorgon. It is particularly valuable to anyone that wishes to visit Cazhaak Draal; while wearing this armor, you have Advantage on saving throws against any magical effect that would cause you to be Restrained or Petrified.

These rations made of troll meat slowly regenerate, promising a long-lasting food supply. A creature can use a Magic action to eat one cake. Eating a cake restores 1 Hit Point, and the cake provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

A pack contains a maximum of 10 cakes. So long as at least 1 cake remains uneaten and unspoiled, the pack regenerates 1d6 cakes per day. If you take Fire or Acid damage while carrying a pack of Grist Cakes, 1d4 cakes permanently spoil and will no longer regenerate.

Hags, oni, doppelgangers, and more all spin webs of intrigue in Droaam, and the richest warlords have found ways to ensure their safety against infiltrators. This 4-inch-diameter, dull-gray glass lens is said to have been ground with a stone fallen from the moon Lharvion. When you speak its command word, the lens' power activates for 1 minute. If you look at a creature through the lens while it is active, you see ghostly images of every shape that creature has taken within the last 24 hours. The lens reveals shapes taken using innate magical abilities, as well as Illusion and Transmutation spells such as Disguise Self and Polymorph. It does not reveal mundane disguises. Once this property is used, it cannot be used again until 7 days have passed.

With the right expertise and rituals, a songbird harpy's magic can be suffused throughout her plumage. While wearing this magical feather, you find that people can be much more agreeable—all they need is a little push. When you make a Charisma (*Persuasion*) check, you can choose to have Advantage on the check (no action required). Once this property is used, the feather loses its luster and becomes nonmagical.

Though most worgs prefer to fight with their teeth or steel jaws, there are those that desire to wield a Dhakaani blade against their enemies. This ornate mask is set with magical gems that focus your subconscious thoughts into a subtle form of telekinesis, allowing you greater control over objects you hold in your teeth.

While wearing the mask, you can use your mouth to wield any Melee weapon that does not have the Heavy, Two-Handed, or Reach properties. If you use the mask to wield a weapon that has Versatile, you can only wield it as if you were using a single hand.

The minotaurs of Droaam have no issues navigating the winding streets of the region's great cities, and their understanding has been captured in these fragile maps. When you speak the map's command word while in the city for which it was made, you can add twice your Proficiency Bonus to any Wisdom (*Survival*) checks made to navigate or track a creature through the city for 1 hour. At the end of the hour, the map crumbles to dust.

Enterprising artificers are keen to bridge the gap between the tallest and the smallest Droaamites. Ogre Tines are just one example of the myriad devices designed to help giantkin interact with kobolds and goblins. Each set consists of five foot-long iron nails bound by a ring at their tops. When held in one hand, the nails can bend and twist as if they were tiny fingers. While using the tines, creatures of Medium size or larger that would normally have Disadvantage on Dexterity (*Sleight of Hand*) checks instead do not have Disadvantage.

This thin rope belt is woven with strands of white and black oni hair. While wearing the belt, you can speak its command word to cause your height to become exactly 5 ft. 10 inches, and your size to become Medium. You can speak the command word again to return to your natural size.

The original Oni Braid was designed by a hobgoblin artificer who wished to see eye to eye with all the people of Droaam, though it's rumored that she designed it to set everyone's height to be one inch less than her own.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these Steel Jaws.

The teeth have 4 charges. When you hit with an attack using them, you can expend 1 charge to leave a set of spectral teeth clamped around the target. The target's Speed is reduced to 0. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a DC 13 Strength saving throw, ending the effect on a success. The teeth regain all expended charges at dawn.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
This 'rope' is made from treated troll entrails. Typically, it is found in a 50-ft length that weighs 6 pounds and can hold up to 3,000 pounds.

If Trollgut Rope is cut, you can use a Magic action to press two ends together, causing them to merge together into a single length of rope. This only works with pieces of Trollgut Rope from the same original coil. If the Trollgut Rope takes Fire or Acid damage, it no longer regenerates and becomes nonmagical.

A Spirit Board is a board with letters, numbers, 'yes', 'no', 'hello', and 'goodbye' written on it. Together with a planchette it is used to communicate with ghosts. A __Spiritualist__ can use it as their Spellcasting Focus
Digital games are a variant of Gaming Sets that can be played on any Arcane Terminal, Datapad, or Gamestation. These games range from arcade-like to immersively realistic.

If you have proficiency with a tool, add your Proficiency Bonus to any ability check you make that uses the tool. If you have proficiency in a skill that's used with that check, you have Advantage on the check too.

This canister of pressurized nanites rapidly repairs damage to ships. The canister weighs 20 pounds and can be used as a Magic action from within or outside a damaged ship. The rarity and number of Mega Hit Points the ship regains vary, as shown on the Shipmending Spray table.

This canister of pressurized nanites rapidly repairs damage to ships. The canister weighs 20 pounds and can be used as a Magic action from within or outside a damaged ship. The ship regains 3d6 Mega Hit Points.

This canister of pressurized nanites rapidly repairs damage to ships. The canister weighs 20 pounds and can be used as a Magic action from within or outside a damaged ship. The ship regains 6d6 Mega Hit Points.

This canister of pressurized nanites rapidly repairs damage to ships. The canister weighs 20 pounds and can be used as a Magic action from within or outside a damaged ship. The ship regains 12d6 Mega Hit Points.

This canister of pressurized nanites rapidly repairs damage to ships. The canister weighs 20 pounds and can be used as a Magic action from within or outside a damaged ship. The ship regains 18d6 Mega Hit Points.

As a Utilize action, you can throw this spherical device up to 30 feet, which detonates in a shimmering 30-foot-radius Sphere on impact. Each creature and object that isn't being worn or carried within the Sphere has the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. The condition ends early immediately for a creature after it makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.
While wearing this fingerless glove, you can cast the __Finger Guns__ cantrip using your spellcasting ability. You can use the mastery property of the Finger Guns while attuned to this item.

As a Utilize action, you can throw this bomb up to 30 feet, where it detonates in a 10-foot-radius Sphere a moment after impact. Each creature within the Sphere must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **3d8** Cold damage and its Speed is 0 and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

This device has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and cast __Levitate__ (DC 13) from it. Instead of the target rising vertically up to 20 feet, it is pulled directly toward the device, levitating in a space of your choice within 5 feet of you.

You can take a Bonus Action to violently repel a levitating target within 5 feet of yourself. In a Zero-Gravity environment, all creatures and objects are considered to be levitating. The target is pushed up to 60 away from you in a direction that you choose, ending the __Levitate__ spell. If the target contact hits an obstacle, both the target and the obstacle take **4d6** damage. The GM decides if this damage is Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

description.name: Upgraded Magic Item
description.value: If you have proficiency in Martial weapons, this item grows in power as you do. The item's save DC increases when you reach character level 5 (DC 15), 11 (DC 17), and 17 (DC 18).

This enormous hammer is the badge of office for a dwarven justicar. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can engage its thrusters to deal an extra **1d4** Bludgeoning damage to the target. This damage is 1d6 if the target is *Bloodied*.

description.name: Upgraded Magic Item
description.value: This weapon grows in power as you do. When you reach character level 5, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This bonus increases by +1 at level 11 (+2) and level 17 (+3).

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
This shoulder strap contains six pouches large enough to hold a potion, grenade, or similarly-sized item within easy reach. It can hold 10 pounds of gear.
Objects viewed through Binoculars are magnified to ten times their size.

Using this handheld device, you can verbally communicate with any creature within 1 mile that also has a Comm Set. A Comm Set can be connected to a headset worn on the ear or can be talked into directly. Its signal can penetrate most barriers, but is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

An Engineer's Pack includes a Backpack, a Comm Set, a Crowbar, a Datapad, a Flashlight, a Hammer, an Igniter, a Life Suit, dozens of assorted nuts and bolts, an Omnitool, 10 rolls of Vent Tape, and a Wristwatch.

A Flare is a foot-long, brightly colored stick with a plastic cap. You can strike the bottom of the Flare as a Utilize action, causing it to burst into a bright, colored flame, matching that of the stick. This flame burns for 10 minutes, emitting a 40-foot radius of Bright Light and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. A Flare can burn underwater and in a vacuum.
A Flashlight produces a 60-foot Cone of Bright Light, and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet. It can provide light for up to 4 hours, after which it must recharge for 8 hours.
A Holster is a specially-made holder which allows a blaster which lacks Two-Handed to be carried on a belt or under the arm.

Potions are often loaded into syringes instead of consumed from a bottle. You can load a potion into a Hypodermic Needle as a Bonus Action and administer it to another creature as a Bonus Action. If the creature is unwilling, it must succeed a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus) to avoid the needle.
An Igniter produces a small flame, which you can use to light a Candle, Torch, or campfire.

An Interface Rig includes everything necessary to connect to a device without an accessible interface: a Datapad accessor loaded with complicated algorithms, a plethora of wires and connectors, and a heavy magnet in case things get dire. An Interface Rig is often necessary to gain unauthorized access to a system.

When you drink this can of sugary liquid as a Utilize action, you feel a rush of energy. For the next hour, your Exhaustion level temporarily decreases by 1, to a minimum of 0. You can only be under the effect of one can of Krash at a time.
This foot-long device records and replays audio, organizing entries by date. It can store up to 72 hours of audio before it automatically begins purging the earliest entries.

A Marine's Pack includes a Backpack, a Bedroll, Binoculars, a Comm Set, a Concussion Grenade, a Crowbar, a Flashlight, an Igniter, a Life Suit, 10 days of Rations, Rope, a Tactical Vest, and a roll of Vent Tape.

This multipurpose gadget contains a plethora of useful tools: small knives of various sizes, a small hammer, screwdrivers, a file, a bottle opener, a small saw, a wrench, a can opener, a wire-cutter, and a small set of pliers.

This handheld scanning device has four prominent sensors (each looking like a small radar dish) on its operating end. When directed at an object within 5 feet as a Utilize action, the device measures and displays many of that object's intrinsic properties, including its temperature, density, boiling point, freezing point, conductivity, and viscosity.
A Researcher's Pack includes a Backpack, Binoculars, a Comm Set, a Datapad, a Flashlight, a Holo-Sphere, a Hypodermic Needle, a Life Suit, a Log Keeper, an Omnitool, a Quadcorder, and a Wristwatch.
Ocoulori Radavitis (called a Roach by many spacers) is an insectlike creature that is consumed to improve the results of a void jump. See the Ships chapter for more details.

A Sling is a strap which attaches to a weapon (usually a blaster) and is worn on the body. When you drop a weapon attached to a sling you are wearing, it falls to your side and continues to hang within reach.

A Spacer's Pack includes a Backpack, a Bandolier, a Comm Set, a Datapad, 2 Flashlights, a Holo-Sphere, an Interface Rig, 2 cans of Krash, a Life Suit, a Log Keeper, an Igniter, an Omnitool, a Quadcorder, 10 rolls of Vent Tape, and a Wristwatch.
A Surveyor's Pack includes a Backpack, a Bandolier, a Bedroll, Binoculars, a Comm Set, a Flashlight, a Log Keeper, an Igniter, a Life Suit, a Quadcorder, 10 days of Rations, Rope, and a Wristwatch.

This light vest is covered in pouches, straps, and holsters. The vest can carry a Melee weapon with the Two-Handed or Versatile property on its back and a Dagger or an Antimatter Dagger on its front. It has two Holsters and one built-in Sling. The Tactical Vest can be worn atop armor.

This durable, adhesive tape is useful for any application that involves sticking two things together. While more creative minds might use large quantities of Vent Tape for other uses, most people use it for quick repairs and affixed Flashlights to blasters in a pinch. A single roll of Vent Tape contains 60 feet of 2-inch wide tape.
A simple device with a simple purpose, this watch reports the time in a way that is consistent with all major galactic factions.

This small metallic disk hums with gravitational energy. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing the mine to a space you can see within 30 feet of you. The mine firmly attaches to any surface it touches. If a creature other than you enters the 5-foot Cube area originating at the top of the mine or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. After 10 minutes, the mine burns out and becomes nonmagical.

This golden holy symbol, blessed by the Sun Above, shields you from death. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while you wear this ankh, roll 4d10. Your Hit Points instead change to the number rolled. The ankh then loses its luster and becomes nonmagical.

description.name: Magic Item Set
description.value: Attuning to this ankh and a Heretical Sunstaff of Ra and Solar Wings of Ra counts as being attuned to a single item. If you are attuned to this ankh and one of these items, the ankh doesn't become nonmagical once used. Instead, it temporarily loses its luster and can't be used again until the next dawn.

Arcane Terminals are essential units of computing in the 'Verse. Most information, from private financial records to a ship's star charts, are stored on such terminals. These terminals weigh 500 pounds and come equipped with a keyboard and monitor.

description.name: Data Storage
description.value: A terminal can store arbitrarily large amounts of data, including text, images, and video. Authorized users can search the terminal's data and the data of any other terminal connected to it as a Utilize action. Typically, Arcane Terminals on populated worlds are connected together in planetary networks ("nets") which allow a user to comb through a vast, encyclopedic collection of knowledge, whereas individual terminals are more focused and may only contain information on a few topics.

description.name: Communication Network.
description.value: If the terminal has an installed antenna, authorized users can interface with it using a Datapad out to a range of 1 mile. Multiple users can communicate with each other within that range, using text, audio, or video.

description.name: Ship Computers and Other Functions.
description.value: Starships generally have an Arcane Terminal aboard to control its sensors and systems. These terminals can also perform tasks such as opening and closing doors of a facility, issuing commands to Constructs, or processing technical data.

description.name: Hacking
description.value: Each terminal generally restricts access to authorized users. A DC 15 Intelligence (*Data*) check can hack a terminal and provide unauthorized access. More secure systems might have higher DCs for this check. See "Intelligence (*Data*)" in the Glossary for the rules on Hacking.
This 4,000-pound bomb is capable of cataclysmic destruction.

description.name: Arming the Warhead
description.value: You can arm the warhead over the course of a minute if you know the warhead's command code and have a specially-made key attuned to it. Once the warhead is armed, you can set its method of detonation: Timed or Impact. If you choose a timed detonation, you enter a delay time of 1 minute, 10 minutes, or 1 hour, after which the warhead detonates. If you choose impact, the bomb lays dormant until it is reduced to 0 Hit Points. The warhead has AC 18, 100 Hit Points (1 Mega Hit Point), and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage.

description.name: Detonation
description.value: When the warhead detonates, most things nearby are instantly vaporized. Within a 10-mile-radius Sphere, each creature and object takes 10d10 + 200 Mega Radiant damage. Each creature outside of the 10-mile-radius Sphere but within a 100-mile-radius Sphere makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or take **10d10 + 50** Radiant damage, or half as much on a successful save. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity. A creature that takes damage from this warhead has the Poisoned condition for 24 hours.
The epicenter of the blast becomes a spherical Dead Magic Zone, ranging from a few dozen feet to several miles in diameter.

Once on each of your turns, when you make a melee attack with this weapon, you can engage its thrusters to strike with extra force. You can lunge up to 15 feet toward your target before making the attack. Doing so doesn't spend movement or provoke Opportunity Attacks. On a hit, the attack deals an extra **1d4** Bludgeoning damage.

description.name: Upgraded Magic Item
description.value: This weapon grows in power as you do. When you reach character level 5, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This bonus increases by +1 at level 11 (+2) and level 17 (+3).

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Cleave
description.value: If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

description.name: The B
description.value: E.G.—short for "Big Effing Gun"—is an experimental weapon of unrivaled power. As a Magic action, you can activate this weapon, creating an explosion of lightning and plasma in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 120 feet. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking **10d10 + 50** Radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Once you use this item, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Blaster Prototype

description.value: Every blaster in the 'Verse, from pocket-sized Phasers to ship-mounted Pulse Cannons, operate on the same basic principle: focusing the energy from an arcane battery through an aperture to create an burst of radiation. However, the progenitor to all blasters predates the invention of arcane batteries, and instead utilized a more potent power source: a mortal soul.

The Blaster Prototype was the magnum opus of legendary dwarven inventor Metzer Glimwrought. As the device neared its completion, Metzer's daughter, Vantha Glimwrought, suddenly took ill and deteriorated quickly. Doctors could furnish no cure and Metzer, desperate, turned to necromancy. Using the ritual that binds a lich's phylactery, Metzer bound his daughter's soul to the prototype, simultaneously forestalling her death and furnishing the blaster with an immense power source.

description.name: Magic Weapon
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is a magic weapon that grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

description.name: Auto-Aim
description.value: If you roll less than 10 on the d20 for an attack roll with the Blaster Prototype, you can replace the roll with a 10. The prototype can choose not to grant this benefit, or to instead replace the roll with a 1 if it believes a target is unsuitable.

description.name: Blaster Mastery
description.value: You can use a Magic action to change the blaster's mastery property to that of any blaster of your choice. You can use the mastery property of the blaster, even if you don't have the Weapon Mastery feature, and it doesn't count against the number of weapons you can use. Once you change the mastery property, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

description.name: Machine Code
description.value: Using its Machine Code (DarkMatter24) language, the Blaster Prototype can cast the __Technomancy__ cantrip.

description.name: Sentience
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is a sentient Chaotic Neutral weapon with an Intelligence of 16, a Wisdom of 10, and a Charisma of 15. It has hearing and Darkvision out to 120 feet.
The prototype speaks Common (XPHB), Dwarvish (XPHB), and Machine Code (DarkMatter24), the native code-language of machines, and it can communicate with its wielder telepathically.

description.name: Personality
description.value: Though the prototype is ageless, its personality belongs to a young woman, Vantha Glimwrought, and speaks in an upbeat, chipper tone. The Prototype urges its user to travel to new places and meet interesting people; likewise, it hates being holstered, hidden away, or ignored. Even in life, Vantha was shut away and built up an insatiable wanderlust.

Vantha has complex feelings about her father, the prototype's inventor. Without question, she's grateful to be alive, but feels like her present, captive circumstances are somehow an extension of her father's overbearing nature, even after his death.
Vantha has reservations about being used on Humanoids and will never fire on a person she deems innocent.

description.name: Destroying the Blaster
description.value: The Blaster Prototype is protected by all manner of enchantments from one of history's most ingenious arcanists, rendering it impervious to damage. However, if the blaster is connected to a sufficiently large power source, like a Class 7 or 8 Dark Matter engine at the moment of a void jump, the power surge would be enough to overload the blaster and destroy it.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Blaster
description.value: A weapon with the Blaster property is a Ranged weapon that requires no ammunition. This property counts as Ammunition.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.
